basic_information.official_title: AN ACT APPROPRIATING THE SUM OF TEN BILLION PESOS (P10,000,000,000.00) FROM THE 2020 AND 2021 SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately upon publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the region

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Appropriates ₱10 billion — ₱5 billion each from the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund — for rebuilding, rehabilitating and developing conflict-affected communities in the Bangsamoro.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The Organic Law provides a Special Development Fund for the region. This act appropriates 2 years of it and directs the money at communities damaged by conflict, under the Bangsamoro Development Plan 2020–2022.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: ₱10 billion becomes available for rebuilding and development, with rules on where infrastructure may be built, mandatory website publication of contracts and costs, monthly and quarterly reporting, and salary suspension for officials who fail to report.
who_will_be_affected: Conflict-affected communities across the BARMM — the stated beneficiaries
Contractors bidding for infrastructure projects, whose winning bids and costs must be published
Ministries and offices implementing projects, and their ministers and web administrators
Anyone wanting to know where ₱10 billion went
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in 2021. Its spending deadlines were later extended by BAA 34 and BAA 51.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: ₱10 billion for conflict-affected communities. Every infrastructure contract, winning bidder and final cost must be posted on the implementing ministry's website — and officials who miss the reports have their salaries suspended.
in_practice: ₱5 billion as the 2020 Special Development Fund and ₱5 billion as the 2021 fund
For the rebuilding, rehabilitation and development of conflict-affected communities in the BARMM
Spending must follow the Bangsamoro Development Plan 2020–2022
Released by the finance ministry directly to implementing ministries, on the Chief Minister's approval and a Special Budget Request

Infrastructure may not be sited in critical geo-hazard areas or no-build zones, must meet structural strength and climate resilience standards, and in protected areas may only proceed if intended to enhance biodiversity
Within 30 days of signing a contract: project title, location, description, detailed budget estimates, winning contractor and bid details must be posted on the ministry's website
Within 30 days of a certificate of completion: the detailed actual cost and any variation orders must be posted
Quarterly financial and physical reports within 30 days of each quarter; monthly financial reports by the 10th of the following month
Failure to report suspends the responsible official's salary until they comply

for_specific_groups.Conflict-affected communities: You are the stated purpose of the fund — rebuilding, rehabilitation and development.
for_specific_groups.Anyone watching procurement: Section 5 is the provision to use. Contract details, the winning contractor, the bid as awarded, the final actual cost and every variation order must all be on the ministry's website, with named officials responsible for compliance.
for_specific_groups.Women: The chairperson of the Bangsamoro Women Commission sits ex officio on the fund's Technical Working Group to ensure programmes are gender-responsive.
for_specific_groups.Communities in hazard zones or protected: Section 4 bars siting in critical geo-hazard areas and no-build zones, and restricts major infrastructure in protected areas to projects intended to enhance biodiversity.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Spending ran from 2021, with deadlines later extended by BAA 34 and BAA 51.
what_you_can_do: Check the implementing ministry's website for the project title, budget estimates, winning contractor and bid — required within 30 days of contract signing
Check again after completion for the detailed actual cost and any variation orders
Ask for the quarterly financial and physical reports, and the monthly financial reports
Ask whether a project site was cleared against the geo-hazard and no-build restrictions
watch_out_for: Section 7 allows changes to project design — scope, location, beneficiaries, implementation period — subject to planning authority endorsement and the Chief Minister's approval, so the project you were told about can lawfully change.
The original spending deadlines were extended twice, by BAA 34 and then BAA 51, which removed the disbursement deadline entirely.
The act does not itself publish anything; it obliges ministries to.

key_terms_explained.Special Development Fund: A dedicated development fund for the region under Section 2, Article XIV of the Organic Law.
key_terms_explained.Approved Budget for the Contract: The government's own cost estimate for a project, against which bids are judged.
key_terms_explained.Variation order: A change to a contract after award, often the point at which costs rise.
key_terms_explained.NIPAS: National Integrated Protected Areas System — the protected-area regime restricting construction.
key_terms_explained.URS: Unified Reporting System, the electronic channel for submitting government reports.
key_terms_explained.TWG: Technical Working Group, which prepares the fund's programme of projects.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Rabi ul Awwal 1, 1443 / 8 October 2021, approved by the Chief Minister on 25 October 2021.

benefits.headline: ₱10 billion for conflict-affected communities, with contracts and final costs required to be published.

direct_benefits.benefit: ₱10 billion for rebuilding, rehabilitation and development
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Through implementing ministries under the Bangsamoro Development Plan

direct_benefits.benefit: Published contract details, winning bidder, actual cost and variation orders
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Implementing ministry's website, within 30 days of contract and of completion

direct_benefits.benefit: Monthly and quarterly financial reporting with a real sanction
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Everyone relying on the reports existing
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Salary suspension applies to officials who fail to comply

for_citizens: None. The duties fall on ministries and officials.
for_ministries: Post contract and cost information on the ministry website within the stated periods
Submit monthly and quarterly financial and physical reports
Ensure infrastructure sites comply with the geo-hazard, climate resilience and protected-area conditions

what_is_prohibited: Siting infrastructure projects in critical geo-hazard areas or no-build zones identified or certified by the environment ministry or other competent authority.
Undertaking major infrastructure within protected areas unless intended to enhance biodiversity.
Failing to submit the required monthly and quarterly reports.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence committed by a member of the public.
penalties.for_officials: Failure to comply with the reporting requirements results in the automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until they comply, under Section 57, Chapter 6, Book VI of Executive Order 292. Repeated failure or refusal without justifiable cause may be a ground for administrative disciplinary action. The act calls this a penal provision and makes the Minister or Head of Office responsible for enforcing it.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The implementing ministry or office, whose minister and web administrator are responsible for compliance with the posting rules
where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which releases the funds and receives the reports; the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority, which reviews the programme of projects
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure, but it creates a large body of documents that must be public.

everyday_scenarios: A road is built in a conflict-affected barangay. Within 30 days of the contract, the ministry must post the project description, the budget estimates, the winning contractor and the bid; within 30 days of completion, the actual cost and any variation orders.
A ministry misses a quarterly report. The responsible official's salary is suspended until it is filed.
A proposed project site sits in a no-build zone. Section 4 bars it — the location must not be in a critical geo-hazard area or no-build zone certified by the environment ministry.
A community is told its project has changed scope. Section 7 permits that, subject to the planning authority's endorsement and the Chief Minister's approval.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Appropriates ₱5,000,000,000 as the 2020 Special Development Fund and ₱5,000,000,000 as the 2021 Special Development Fund, pursuant to Section 2, Article XIV of Republic Act 11054, the Bangsamoro Organic Law.

Section 2 — The amounts are to be used for the rebuilding, rehabilitation and development of conflict-affected communities in the BARMM, in accordance with the Bangsamoro Development Plan 2020–2022 as adopted by the Bangsamoro Economic and Development Council on 5 June 2020 and by the BTA Parliament on 3 July 2020. Releases are made by the MFBM directly to implementing ministries and offices, subject to the Chief Minister's approval and submission of a Special Budget Request with supporting documents.

Section 3 — Cash budgeting: appropriations are available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2022. Infrastructure capital outlays are obligable to that date with completion, inspection and payment by 30 June 2023; MOOE and other capital outlays likewise obligable to that date with delivery, inspection and payment by 31 March 2023.

Section 4 — Additional requirements for infrastructure: sites must not lie in critical geo-hazard areas or no-build zones identified or certified by the Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy or another competent authority; construction standards must follow Ministry of Public Works rules considering structural strength and climate resilience; and projects within the National Integrated Protected Area System must minimise biodiversity loss, with major infrastructure permitted there only if intended to enhance biodiversity. The MPW shall consider climate data, risk assessment and green building standards in planning, designing, constructing, engineering and renovating government buildings and facilities.

Section 5 — Transparency in infrastructure projects: ministries and offices shall post on their websites the project title, location and detailed description, the detailed estimates behind the Approved Budget for the Contract, and the winning contractor with the detailed estimates of the bid as awarded, within 30 calendar days of entering into the contract; and the detailed actual cost and any variation orders within 30 calendar days of the certificate of completion. Ministers, heads of offices and web administrators are responsible for compliance.

Section 6 — Reporting: quarterly financial and physical accomplishment reports within 30 days of each quarter, via the Unified Reporting System, in hard copy to the MFBM and on the ministry's website, with written notice of submission. Failure results in automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until compliance, under Section 57, Chapter 6, Book VI of E.O. 292; repeated failure may ground administrative disciplinary action, and the Minister or Head of Office is responsible for enforcing this penal provision. Monthly financial reports on appropriations, allotments, obligations and disbursements are due by the 10th day of the following month through the same three channels.

Section 7 — Implementing agencies are given maximum flexibility in the use of cash allocations provided the authorised allotment for a specific purpose is not exceeded, including adjustments to project design for changes in scope, location, beneficiaries and implementation period, subject to the endorsement of the Director General of the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority and the approval of the Chief Minister.

Section 8 — Creates a Special Development Fund Technical Working Group chaired by the Senior Minister, with members determined by the Chief Minister and the BPDA as Secretariat. To ensure programmes, projects and activities are gender-responsive, the chairperson of the Bangsamoro Women Commission is an ex officio member. The TWG consolidates the programme of projects and submits it to the BPDA for review against the Bangsamoro Development Plan, and the BPDA Director General submits it for the Chief Minister's approval.
Section 11 — Takes effect immediately upon publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the region.

citizen_questions.q: How much money is this, and what is it for?
citizen_questions.a: ₱10 billion — ₱5 billion each from the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund — for the rebuilding, rehabilitation and development of conflict-affected communities in the BARMM.

citizen_questions.q: Can I find out who won a contract and what it cost?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 5 requires the implementing ministry to post the project description, budget estimates, winning contractor and bid on its website within 30 days of signing, and the detailed actual cost and any variation orders within 30 days of completion.

citizen_questions.q: What happens if a ministry does not report?
citizen_questions.a: The responsible official's salary is automatically suspended until they comply, and repeated refusal can be a ground for administrative disciplinary action.

citizen_questions.q: Can a project be built anywhere?
citizen_questions.a: No. Sites must not be in critical geo-hazard areas or no-build zones, construction must meet structural strength and climate resilience standards, and major infrastructure in protected areas is allowed only if intended to enhance biodiversity.

citizen_questions.q: Can the project I was promised change?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 7 allows adjustments in scope, location, beneficiaries and implementation period, provided the authorised allotment is not exceeded, with the planning authority's endorsement and the Chief Minister's approval.

citizen_questions.q: Is there anything on women's participation?
citizen_questions.a: The chairperson of the Bangsamoro Women Commission is an ex officio member of the fund's Technical Working Group, expressly to ensure programmes are gender-responsive.
